title: Tenant scaling budget advisor and predictive cooldown policy
author: Jordan Li
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets require more predictable per-tenant throughput while still allowing controlled bursts. Current autoscaler hysteresis and global headroom heuristics lead to noisy tenant-level oscillation for low-volume tenants and delayed recovery for tenants that briefly spike. This PR introduces two complementary features: 1) a per-tenant scaling budget advisor that computes an explicit short-term token budget and burn-rate estimate for each tenant and exposes it to the autoscaler and routing layer; 2) a predictive cooldown policy that uses an exponential decaying forecast of recent burst activity to decide cooldown windows and avoid premature upscales.

High-level design: - Budget advisor runs as part of the fleet controller reconciliation loop; it aggregates recent per-tenant allocation, completed requests, and queued requests over sliding windows (1m/5m/15m) and outputs: tenant_scaling_budget_estimate (tokens/min), budget_confidence (0..1), and recommended_max_burst_tokens. - Predictive cooldown uses a lightweight AR(1)-like forecast on the burn-rate plus a volatility factor derived from percentiles (p50/p95) to produce predictive_cooldown_seconds; the autoscaler respects this cooldown per-tenant and will not aggressively shrink reserved capacity below the advised budget during the cooldown. - API/Config: new dedicated config section dedicated.scaling.advisor.enabled (bool), dedicated.scaling.advisor.window_seconds (int), dedicated.scaling.predictive_cooldown.enabled (bool), and a per-tenant override map.

Metrics and telemetry: added tenant_scaling_budget_estimate, tenant_budget_burn_rate, tenant_budget_confidence, tenant_predictive_cooldown_seconds, and advisor_reconciliations_total; these wire into the Console per-tenant dashboard and to the existing utilization sampler to enable historical analysis. Compatibility: no breaking API changes; defaults are backward-compatible (both features disabled by default).

Testing and rollout: feature gated behind dedicated.scaling.advisor.enabled; unit tests for advisor math and e2e test that simulates intermittent spikes; staged rollout: opt-in via config for a small number of fleets, monitor advisor_reconciliations_total and budget_confidence distribution. See linear items ENG-1842 and ENG-1987 for evaluation criteria and rollout playbook.

Commits summary: - Initial advisor skeleton, reconciliation loop, and metrics registration - Add budget estimator algorithm and windowed aggregators - Wire advisor output into autoscaler decision path and routing token pool - Predictive cooldown implementation and per-tenant override plumbing - Tests: unit tests for estimator, integration e2e for burst behavior - Docs: ops runbook and telemetry dashboard notes - CI and small fixes after reviewer feedback

Changes (high-level files touched): pkg/autoscaler/advisor.go, pkg/autoscaler/estimator.go, pkg/autoscaler/predictive_cooldown.go, pkg/telemetry/metrics_registry.go, cmd/agent/main.go (config wiring), charts/dedicated/values.yaml (feature flags), docs/ops/tenant-scaling.md, tests/e2e/tenant_budget_test.go.

Review conversation highlights: - Priya: "Can you show a comparison of p50/p95 advisor outputs for 1k tenant sample? Concerned about false confidence in low-signal cases." Jordan: "Added budget_confidence and lowered weighting on single-sample spikes; pushed a unit test and a small script (tests/tools/generate_tenant_signals.go) used in the benchmark." - Evan: "We need a clear abort path if advisor metrics cause autoscaler regressions in production." Jordan: "Added an autoscaler circuit-breaker check that ignores advisor_reconciliations_total < 50 or budget_confidence < 0.2; documented behavior in the runbook." - Marta: "How will this interact with reserved capacity and burst token pools?" Jordan: "Advisor emits recommended_max_burst_tokens which the routing layer uses to prioritize token assignment; for fleets with reserved capacity the advisor is advisory only unless the fleet config opts-in to advisory_enforced=true."

CI notes: initial CI run showed a flaky e2e related to timing; re-ran the e2e with extended timeouts and all checks passed: unit tests (pass), lint (pass), build (pass), e2e (pass on rerun). Merge outcome: squashed and merged to main; small follow-ups planned to tune default windows.

Release notes: - New: per-tenant scaling budget advisor (opt-in) that estimates short-term token budgets and exposes burn-rate and confidence metrics. - New: predictive cooldown policy to reduce thrash after transient spikes. - Observability: new per-tenant metrics and Console dashboard additions.

Rollout/ops: disabled by default; enable via charts/dedicated/values.yaml: dedicated.scaling.advisor.enabled=true and monitor advisor_reconciliations_total and tenant_budget_confidence. Related: ENG-1842 (evaluation harness), ENG-1987 (runbook and dashboard).
